To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
prolonged growth in hypoxic environments activates the hif- 1 pathway in multiple tissues and reorganizes a neuronal circuit for behavioral oxygen preference in Caenorhabdtis elegans.
prolonged exposure to hypoxia alters oxygen preference in C. elegans by activating the hifi pathway, which transforms a regulated neuronal network into a smaller, constitutively active circuit.
the hif- 1 pathway reorganizes the neuronal circuitry for oxygen preference in C. elegans.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of oxygen preference in the nematodes C. elegans and C. briggsae.
the mechanisms by which the nervous system senses oxygen and how these mechanisms change in response to hypoxia.
understanding the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying oxygen sensing and the role of oxygen sensing in the control of behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the HIF- 1 pathway is activated by hypoxia in neurons and gonadal endocrine tissues, and this activation reconfigures a distributed, regulated neural network into a smaller fixed network that is active at a lower oxygen level.
the HIF-2 pathway acts in both neurons and in gonad endocrine cells to reorganize the neural circuit for oxygen preference.
the HIF- 1 pathway reorganizes the neural circuit for oxygen preference to generate adaptive behavioral changes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hypoxia, through HIF-1, reprograms the oxygen preference circuit of C. elegans.
hypoxia and the hif- 1 pathway can reorganize a neural circuit for oxygen-dependent behavioral responses.
the HIF pathway is not just a transcriptional pathway that regulates gene expression, but it also regulates neuronal circuits and behavioral output in a physiological manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hypoxic adaptation is not only a cellular response but also involves reorganization of a neural circuit to modify behavioral oxygen preference.
the hypoxia response in C. elegans is not just a response to a stress but rather an adaptive change to a changing environment.
the HIF- pathway is involved in the regulation of oxygen preference behavior.
